title: GuestConfig
description:
The configuration structure for the guest VM serialized from a toml file provided by user,
and then converted to `AxVMConfig` for the VM creation.

base.description: The base configuration for the VM.

devices.description: The devices configuration for the VM.

kernel.description: The kernel configuration for the VM.

GuestDevices.description:
User-selectable physical-device configuration.

Virtual platform devices, including the serial port and interrupt
controller, are selected by the machine profile and never appear here.

disabled.description:
Physical devices removed from a passthrough guest's default assignment.

The root baseline selector `/` is not valid here. An empty `passthrough`
list still keeps the baseline; starting from no physical devices requires
`guest_type = "virtualized"`.

passthrough.description: Physical devices explicitly assigned to the guest.

virtual.description: Virtual devices instantiated through the code-registered model catalog.

GuestType.description:
Determines how the guest receives physical devices.

Virtualized guests start with no physical-device mappings. Passthrough
guests start with all guest-assignable physical devices and then remove the
devices listed in [`GuestDevices::disabled`].

oneOf.description: Only explicitly selected physical devices are mapped into the guest.
All guest-assignable physical devices are mapped unless disabled.

PhysicalDeviceRef.description:
A structured reference to a host physical device.

The initial selector is an absolute device-tree path. Raw addresses and IRQ
numbers deliberately are not part of the user-facing configuration.

path.description:
Absolute device-tree path identifying the physical device, or `/` for
the root baseline a `passthrough` guest already starts from. `/` is only
valid in the `passthrough` list of a passthrough guest.

VMBaseConfig.description: The configuration structure for the guest VM base info.

guest_type.description: Guest address-space and physical-device assignment model.

phys_cpu_ids.description:
The physical CPU ids.
- if `phys_cpu_sets` is `Some`, these are the guest-visible vCPU ids.
- otherwise, these select host CPU identities and also become the guest IDs.

Some ARM platforms will provide a specified cpu hw id in the device tree, which is
read from `MPIDR_EL1` register (probably for clustering).

phys_cpu_sets.description:
The final host affinity mask for each vCPU.

- If `None`, vcpu will be scheduled on available physical CPUs randomly.
- If set, each vcpu will be scheduled on the specified physical CPUs.

  FDT-backed AArch64 and RISC-V paths require one mask per `phys_cpu_ids` entry;
  each mask must be non-zero, fit the host CPU width, and select one host CPU.
  Other scheduler paths may support masks selecting multiple physical CPUs.

VMKernelConfig.description: The configuration structure for the guest VM kernel.

bios_load_addr.description: The load address of the BIOS image, `None` if not used.

bios_path.description: The file path of the BIOS image, `None` if not used.

boot_protocol.description:
Guest boot protocol. When omitted, `enable_bios` selects `multiboot`;
otherwise direct boot is used.

cmdline.description: The command line of the kernel.

dtb_load_addr.description: The load address of the device tree blob (DTB), `None` if not used.

dtb_path.description: The file path of the device tree blob (DTB), `None` if not used.

enable_bios.description: Whether to enable BIOS boot flow for this VM.

entry_point.description: The entry point of the kernel image.

kernel_load_addr.description: The load address of the kernel image.

kernel_path.description: The file path of the kernel image.

ramdisk_load_addr.description: The load address of the ramdisk image, `None` if not used.

ramdisk_path.description: The file path of the ramdisk image, `None` if not used.

uefi_firmware_path.description: The file path of the UEFI firmware image, `None` if not used.
